document.title: Attention mechanism, understand it step by step

attrs.name: Attention mechanism, understand it step by step

content.text: Read the following sentence and you will immediately know that "it" refers to animals; replace "tired" with "wide" and "it" becomes the road.
Transformer relies on the attention mechanism to do the same thing: each word scores all other words, converts the scores into weights, and then mixes their information according to the weights.

props.title: Where do you look at each word?
props.introduction: Click on any word to see who it gives attention to. Then switch to the end of the sentence and see how "it" changes its mind.

labels.hint: The attention of "{word}" is being displayed: the thicker the arc and the darker the word block, the more weight it will be assigned.
labels.lowNote: The temperature is low: the word with the highest score takes almost all the weight; if it drops further, softmax will only select one word.
labels.midNote: T = 1 is just a plain softmax: each word is assigned a small weight, which always adds up to 100%.
labels.highNote: High temperature: The gap between scores is reduced, the weight tends to be average, and each word is about {even}.
labels.note: The scores are manually set for explanation and do not come from the trained model; the calculation of softmax is accurate. Real attention doesn’t have a temperature knob, and that’s what “divide by √d” in step 3 below does.

content.text: Calculate it step by step
There's just a little bit of calculation behind those arcs. Next, use the small numbers that can be checked by hand to go through it completely.

props.title: Q · Kᵀ → ÷ √d → softmax → × V
props.introduction: Three words, vectors of length 4, all small integers. Choose a word to read and click on it step by step.

steps.title: Each word carries three vectors
steps.body: The word vectors are multiplied by the three learned matrices respectively to obtain the query Q, key K and value V. Here we start directly from the result of the multiplication.

steps.title: Score in pairs
steps.body: Do a dot product for each query and each key. A large dot product indicates that the two vectors are in the same direction: "This is exactly the word I am looking for."

steps.title: reduce the fraction
steps.body: The longer the vector (the larger d), the larger the dot product. Divide by √d to keep the score within the appropriate range so that softmax will not focus on just one word - the effect is the same as turning up the temperature above.

steps.title: Convert scores into weights
steps.body: softmax takes the exponent of e for each score and divides it by the sum of the entire row: each weight is positive and each row adds up to 1.

steps.title: Mix vector of values ​​by weight
steps.body: The output for each word is the weighted average of all value vectors. "It" results mostly from "animals" - that's what "attention" means.

labels.inputs: Input · d = 4 (V only uses 2 numbers for easy calculation)
labels.rowSum: The sum of each row is 1

meanings.q: Query: What is this word looking for.
meanings.k: Key: How this word can be found.
meanings.v: Value: The content handed over when selected.

content.text: Together it is one line:
Attention(Q, K, V) = softmax(Q·Kᵀ ÷ √d) · V
. That's the whole mechanism, and the rest of the Transformer is built around it.
The position of attention in Transformer
Transformer is built by stacking many identical blocks. Attention is the only link in exchanging information between words; the subsequent feed-forward network processes each word individually.

content.text: Common misunderstandings
Go step by step to see what actually happened.

attrs.title: "Attention weights explain why the model decides the way it does."

content.text: Not reliable. A weight only indicates how many value vectors of a certain word are mixed into a certain head of a certain layer, and the model has many layers and many heads. Jain and Wallace found that widely different weights can produce the same predictions
; Wiegreffe and Pinter believe that weights still carry useful signals
. Think of it as a clue, not an explanation.

attrs.title: “Each word only focuses on the other word.”

content.text: softmax assigns a positive weight to each word, which always adds up to 1 for each row. Weights may be focused, but attention is a blend, not a pointer.

attrs.title: "Q, K, V are three different inputs."

content.text: In self-attention, all three come from the same set of word vectors X, but are multiplied by three different learning matrices:
Q = X·W_Q,  K = X·W_K,  V = X·W_V
. The matrices are different, and the words "what you are looking for" and "what you can provide" can be different.

attrs.title: "Attention itself knows the order of words."

content.text: It doesn't know it itself: if the words are scrambled, the output of each word will be exactly the same, but the position will be changed. The order information comes from the position encoding added to the word vector before entering the first block.

attrs.title: “There is only one mode of attention on one level.”

content.text: The original Transformer ran 8 heads in parallel per layer, each with its own smaller Q, K, V (64 numbers per word instead of 512). Different heads can learn different relationships
